title: What does Japan's PMD Act require of pharmacy managers and pharmacy staff training?
description: Japan's PMD Act and ordinances on pharmacy managers: duties, written opinions, the 2021 compliance system, and mandatory staff training on dispensing safety.
shortAnswer: Under Japan's PMD Act, every pharmacy must be run day to day by a pharmacist manager with the ability and experience for the role, who supervises staff and gives the pharmacy founder written opinions. Since August 1, 2021, founders must run a legal compliance system that includes training for responsible officers and staff. A separate MHLW ordinance requires guidelines and staff training on dispensing safety, information provision and drug sales.
keyTakeaways: Article 7 of the PMD Act requires a pharmacist to manage each pharmacy on site, and since August 1, 2021 requires the manager to have the ability and experience needed to perform the statutory duties.

Article 8 makes the manager responsible for supervising pharmacists and other staff and for giving the founder written opinions; Article 11 of the Enforcement Regulation requires copies of those opinions to be kept for three years.

Article 9-2 and Article 15-11-2 of the Enforcement Regulation require the founder's legal compliance system to include education and training of officers and staff responsible for pharmaceutical affairs, with its implementation evaluated.

Article 1 of the pharmacy operating system ordinance (MHW Ordinance No. 3 of 1964) requires guidelines and staff training on dispensing safety, dispensing management and drug sales, with a drug safety responsible person and written procedures.
From May 20, 2027, pharmacies that entrust over-the-counter drug handover to registered handover stores or outsource specified dispensing work gain additional training duties.
regulator: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) Pharmaceutical Safety Bureau, with prefectural governors licensing and inspecting pharmacies
appliesTo: Pharmacy founders (yakkyoku kaisetsusha), including corporate chains and their officers responsible for pharmaceutical affairs
Pharmacy managers (yakkyoku no kanrisha), who must be pharmacists
Pharmacists, registered sellers and other pharmacy staff
Drug safety responsible persons appointed under the pharmacy operating system ordinance

sections.heading: Which laws set pharmacy manager and staff training duties?

blocks.text: Three instruments work together. The **Act on Securing Quality, Efficacy and Safety of Products Including Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices** (医薬品医療機器等法, the PMD Act, Act No. 145 of 1960) sets the manager's role and the founder's compliance system in Articles 7 to 9-2 ([PMD Act, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/335AC0000000145)). The **PMD Act Enforcement Regulation** (医薬品医療機器等法施行規則, MHW Ordinance No. 1 of 1961) fills in the manager's duties and the compliance system ([Enforcement Regulation, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/336M50000100001)). The **Ordinance Establishing the Operating Systems of Pharmacies, Store-based Sellers and Household Distributors** (薬局並びに店舗販売業及び配置販売業の業務を行う体制を定める省令, MHW Ordinance No. 3 of 1964) sets the operating system standard, including staff training ([operating system ordinance, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/339M50000100003)).

The operating system standard is a license condition. Article 5(2) of the PMD Act allows the prefectural governor to refuse a pharmacy license where the dispensing and sales operating system does not meet the ordinance standard, and Article 72-2 lets the governor order a licensed pharmacy that falls below the standard to put its system right.

sections.heading: Who must manage a pharmacy, and what must the manager do?

blocks.text: A pharmacist must manage every pharmacy on site. Under Article 7, a founder who is a pharmacist manages the pharmacy personally unless it designates another pharmacist working there; a founder who is not a pharmacist must designate one. Article 7(3) requires the manager to have the ability and experience needed to perform the statutory duties, and Article 7(4) bars the manager from managing or doing pharmaceutical work elsewhere without the governor's permission.

Article 8 sets the duties. The manager must supervise the pharmacists and other staff working in the pharmacy, manage its structure and equipment and its drugs and other goods, and take necessary care in its operations so that no harm to public health arises (paragraph 1). The manager must give the founder necessary opinions in writing to prevent harm to public health (paragraph 2).

Article 11 of the Enforcement Regulation adds that the manager's duties include exercising the authority the founder gives under the compliance system, confirming drug test results, keeping the required books and preserving records, and that the manager must take measures needed to secure the pharmacy's cybersecurity and keep copies of written opinions to the founder for three years.

Article 9(2) closes the loop: a founder that has designated a manager must respect the manager's written opinions and, where measures are needed for legal compliance, take them and record what was done, or record that nothing was done and why. Article 73 lets the governor order a change of manager where the manager breaches pharmaceutical law or is found unsuitable.

sections.heading: What training does the 2021 legal compliance system require?

blocks.text: Since August 1, 2021, Article 9-2 of the PMD Act has required every pharmacy founder to take three kinds of measures to secure compliance with pharmaceutical law: clarify the manager's authority, build systems to ensure lawful operations and supervise responsible officers and staff, and take other measures such as issuing compliance guidelines to staff. The founder must record the measures and keep the records. Comparing the e-Gov versions of the Act on July 31 and August 1, 2021 confirms that Article 9-2, the manager competence requirement in Article 7(3) and the written opinion duties in Articles 8(2) and 9(2) all took effect on that date.

Article 15-11-2 of the Enforcement Regulation specifies the system. Item 2(a) requires a system for preparing the rules needed to keep operations lawful, for **implementing and evaluating education and training** for officers and staff responsible for pharmaceutical affairs, and for creating, managing and keeping records of operations. Item 1 requires the manager's authority over instructing and supervising pharmacists and other staff to be made clear. Item 3 requires compliance guidelines for staff and, for founders holding two or more pharmacy licenses, measures to confirm that every pharmacy's compliance system works, including defining the role of any person who assists the founder in overseeing multiple sites.

sections.heading: What staff training does the operating system ordinance require?

blocks.text: Article 1(1) of the operating system ordinance contains three training items for pharmacies:

blocks.caption: Training items in Article 1(1) of the pharmacy operating system ordinance (MHW Ordinance No. 3 of 1964), as at November 2026
head: Item
Purpose
Required measures
rows: Guidelines, staff training and other necessary measures
Appropriate management of dispensing, including information provision and guidance to patients and storage of drugs for dispensing
Guidelines, staff training and other necessary measures
Appropriate management of drug sales, including information provision, storage and responses outside opening hours, for pharmacies that sell drugs
Guidelines, staff training, including training on specified (online and telephone) sales where the pharmacy does them, and other necessary measures

blocks.text: Article 1(2) lists what those measures must include: a responsible person for the safe use of drugs; an accident reporting system from staff to the founder; restricting who may enter drug storage areas; written procedures for drug safety, information provision and guidance, and dispensing and sales management, including procedures for designated abuse-prone drugs; procedures for any pharmacist absence time; and improvement measures based on information collected. The procedures and the accident reports are natural sources for training content.

Neither the ordinance nor the Enforcement Regulation sets a training frequency. The founder should define one in its guidelines and justify it by role and by changes to procedures, as with any [mandatory training](/glossary/mandatory-training) program.

MHLW Ordinance No. 110 of 2026 amends the operating system ordinance from **May 20, 2027**, implementing a stage of the 2025 PMD Act amendment. Comparing the current and future versions on e-Gov, the changes add training duties for two new business models:

items: pharmacies that entrust the handover of over-the-counter drugs to registered handover stores (tōroku ukewatashi tenpo) must prepare guidelines on the stores' operations and drug management, and train staff of both the pharmacy and the handover store, with item (xiv) training extended to the handover entrustment; and
pharmacies that outsource, or accept, specified dispensing work must prepare outsourcing or acceptance procedures, and a pharmacy accepting such work must appoint a responsible person for it.

blocks.text: Article 7 of the Act is also amended from that date so the manager's role extends to managing handover at registered handover stores, and Article 8 gains a duty for the manager to respect the opinions of the handover manager. As at November 2026, these changes are promulgated but not in force.

blocks.text: Prefectural governors enforce through on-site inspections and orders. Article 72-2 allows an order to bring the operating system back up to the ordinance standard. Article 72-2-2 allows an order to improve a compliance system under Article 9-2 that is insufficient. Article 73 allows an order to change the manager, and Article 75 allows license revocation or business suspension for violations of pharmaceutical law. For pharmacist professional development, which is outside the PMD Act, compare [US pharmacist continuing education](/regulations/pharmacist-continuing-education-requirements-us) and [Australian pharmacist CPD](/regulations/pharmacist-cpd-requirements-australia).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the Act's manager and compliance articles, the Enforcement Regulation and the operating system ordinance as linked obligations per pharmacy, then connects them to each pharmacy's procedures and accident reports. Learning outcomes and assessments are defined before content, and the May 2027 changes can be entered as dated obligations for sites that adopt the new models.

faqs.q: Must a pharmacy manager in Japan be a pharmacist?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 7 of the PMD Act requires the pharmacy to be managed on site by a pharmacist, either the founder personally or a pharmacist designated from those working at the pharmacy. Since August 1, 2021 the manager must also have the ability and experience needed for the statutory duties.

faqs.q: How often must pharmacy staff be trained in Japan?
faqs.a: No frequency is set in the PMD Act, the Enforcement Regulation or the operating system ordinance. They require training as part of guidelines and systems that the founder designs. The founder should state a frequency in its guidelines and show that training follows procedure changes and accident findings.

faqs.q: How long must a pharmacy manager's written opinions be kept?
faqs.a: Three years. Article 11(2)(ii) of the Enforcement Regulation requires the manager to keep copies of the written opinions given to the founder under Article 8(2) of the Act for three years. The founder must separately record the measures it took in response.

faqs.q: Does the compliance system apply to independent single pharmacies?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 9-2 applies to every pharmacy founder. The extra multi-site measures in Article 15-11-2(3) apply only to founders holding two or more pharmacy licenses, but the training, rules and records system in item 2 applies to all founders.
